'''Richard Garfield''' designed ''Magic: The Gathering'' (1993), the first collectible card game.<ref name="wp-garfield">[https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Garfield Richard Garfield], Wikipedia. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261010202730/https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Garfield Internet Archive].</ref> [[Tom Braunlich]] and [[Rollie Tesh]] met him on Bainbridge Island, near Wizards of the Coast, while they designed Decipher's [[Star Trek CCG]]. They told Wizards they would not copy ''Magic''.<ref name="bp27">[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zK_94pNOPTU&t=546s The Booster Pack #27 — The making of the Star Trek CCG with Tom Braunlich], The Booster Pack Network (10 August 2022), 9:06–10:30. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20221006131804/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zK_94pNOPTU Internet Archive].</ref> After Lucasfilm moved the ''Star Wars'' card-game license from [[Decipher]] to Wizards of the Coast, Garfield designed the ''[[Star Wars Trading Card Game]]'' (2002).<ref name="wp-swtcg">[https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Star_Wars_Trading_Card_Game Star Wars Trading Card Game], Wikipedia. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20260202232757/https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Star_Wars_Trading_Card_Game Internet Archive].</ref>

== Meeting Decipher's designers ==

Braunlich and Tesh heard about ''Magic'' from another inventor and met Wizards of the Coast "a couple of times". They saw that a strong license with an original gameplay system "would have a natural."<ref name="rfd14">[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ZsJ-sWiL1Iw&t=279s Broadcast 14 – Radio Free Decipher (16 April 1999): Rollie Tesh, Tom Braunlich (Part 1)], Decipher; posted by Player's Council (aired 16 April 1999), 4:39–6:44. Preserved copy: [https://archive.org/details/youtube-ZsJ-sWiL1Iw Internet Archive]. Transcript: [[Radio Free Decipher/Episode 14 transcript]].</ref> Because they lived on Bainbridge Island near Wizards, they met Garfield and "assured them we weren't gonna copy".<ref name="bp27" />

Braunlich said their aim was "to not copy what Magic: The Gathering was doing, but have a game that really captured the essence of these licenses."<ref name="ringer">Ben Lindbergh, [https://www.theringer.com/2018/5/21/17374528/star-wars-customizable-card-game-player-community The Force Is Strong With This 'Star Wars' Subculture], ''The Ringer'' (21 May 2018). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20241203024546/https://www.theringer.com/2018/5/21/17374528/star-wars-customizable-card-game-player-community Internet Archive].</ref> See [[Inspirations for Star Wars CCG#Magic: The Gathering]].

== Star Wars Trading Card Game ==

Wizards of the Coast published the ''[[Star Wars Trading Card Game]]'' from April 2002. Garfield designed it. It used all-new mechanics and was not compatible with Star Wars CCG.<ref name="icv2-2002">[https://icv2.com/articles/games/view/983/wizards-coast-gets-star-wars-ccg Wizards of the Coast Gets Star Wars CCG], ICv2 (1 January 2002). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261008201620/https://icv2.com/articles/games/view/983/wizards-coast-gets-star-wars-ccg Internet Archive].</ref><ref name="wp-swtcg" />

SWCCG players [[Jonny Chu]] and [[Paul Todd Feldman]] playtested it at Wizards. Chu said the testers met Garfield. The players told Wizards they would not play the game.<ref name="chu">[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=JLkMOP3rLQ8&t=1072s SWCCG PDS2: Jonny Chu Interview & HB X-wings], Bill Bisco, YouTube (28 April 2025), 17:52–19:04.</ref><ref name="torch">[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=b9f9tNBiU2I&t=207s SWCCG PDS2: DRTORCH Worlds Finalist 1996,1997,1999,2000 Interview, MWYHL 2Test], Bill Bisco, YouTube (29 May 2025), 3:27–4:10. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20260929064953/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=b9f9tNBiU2I Internet Archive].</ref>
